purpose: Research record for two distinct browser-agent implementation guides: locating controls across open Shadow DOM boundaries and selecting dates in native versus application-built pickers.

topicSelection.searchMethod: Public web search via the available web search tool, followed by opening the selected public pages. Search result totals and provider-side query volume were not exposed.

queries.query: site:stackoverflow.com/questions Playwright shadow DOM locator closed shadow root
queries.observedRelevantResult: A Playwright locator issue report about a shadow DOM slot selector (issue #33547; version 1.48.2).

queries.query: site:stackoverflow.com/questions Playwright date picker calendar input type date
queries.observedRelevantResult: A Stack Overflow question asks how to inspect the native HTML date picker DOM; one public answer distinguishes application form input from the browser-owned picker UI. The question has no accepted answer.
Current Playwright locator documentation states default Shadow DOM behavior and the XPath and closed-root exceptions.

queries.query: site:developer.mozilla.org input type date value locale
queries.observedRelevantResult: MDN documents locale-dependent display and normalized yyyy-mm-dd value for the native date input.

queries.query: WAI ARIA APG date picker dialog example keyboard accessible
queries.observedRelevantResult: W3C APG provides a date-picker dialog example with a grid, keyboard behavior, focus management, and an explicit example-only implementation warning.

publicDemandSignals.signal: Playwright GitHub issue #33547 was opened 2024-11-11 for version 1.48.2. The author reported a timeout when a direct-child CSS selector crossed a slot and said a descendant selector worked in that reproduction. The issue is closed. This is a historical, version-specific developer report; it does not establish a current general Playwright bug or indicate search volume.
publicDemandSignals.articleIntent: Diagnose the DOM boundary and choose supported locators across open roots; distinguish XPath, slot, closed-root, iframe, and agent-interface limits.

publicDemandSignals.signal: The Stack Overflow question 'How to inspect the dom of the HTML date picker calendar?' has a public answer recommending filling a date input when the application behavior, rather than the browser's own picker UI, is under test. It was answered 2024-09-21 and edited 2024-09-23. The result page shows an answer score of 4 at observation time; no query volume or search-result total was exposed.
publicDemandSignals.articleIntent: Choose an appropriate path for native date inputs versus custom calendar widgets and verify the accepted value without assuming a universal picker API.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Locators
factsUsed: Playwright locators work with Shadow DOM by default
XPath does not pierce shadow roots
Closed-mode shadow roots are not supported
Locators are strict for single-element actions

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Other locators
factsUsed: Playwright CSS selectors pierce open shadow DOM
User-facing locators are preferred over structure-dependent CSS

officialTechnicalSources.title: MDN: <input type="date">
factsUsed: The native date input value is normalized to yyyy-mm-dd
The displayed format varies with browser locale
The control supports min, max, and step constraints

officialTechnicalSources.title: W3C WAI ARIA APG: Date picker dialog example
factsUsed: Illustrative dialog and grid structure for a custom date picker
Keyboard behavior and focus management example
The example warns that it is not production code and requires support testing

claimsAndBoundaries: Playwright examples are scoped to the documented JavaScript API; no compatibility claim is made for Browser Use, arbitrary MCP servers, other agents, or every browser integration.
Open and closed Shadow DOM behavior, XPath limitations, and slot diagnostics are attributed to Playwright documentation and a historical, closed issue. No current defect is inferred from the issue.
The yyyy-mm-dd value applies to the HTML date input. It does not define custom widget formats, native picker DOM, server acceptance, or successful form submission.
The W3C APG calendar is an illustrative accessibility pattern, not a required implementation or a certification of a production widget.

The offline synthetic fixture executed successfully for its listed local assertions only. This does not establish browser-agent or LLM performance, compatibility beyond the recorded environment, or behavior on production forms. Other picker implementations, locale configurations, and Shadow DOM structures are outside the fixture scope.
